questions.explain: To show an LWC inside a site that isn't on Salesforce, use **Lightning Out** (Lightning Out 2.0, or the older beta). The outside app handles sign-in, which the portal already does through OAuth.
wrong: CSP Trusted Sites let Salesforce pages reach other domains, not outside sites host Salesforce components.
`apex:includeLightning` is a Visualforce tag; it can't run in a Node.js page.
An Experience Cloud site is a separate Salesforce site; it doesn't embed into the Node.js portal.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Use Components Outside Salesforce with Lightning Out 2.0

questions.q: In a Lightning console app, an LWC in the utility bar publishes the selected customer on a message channel. A second LWC sits on the Account record page, which agents usually keep open in several workspace tabs. Only the subscriber in the focused tab updates, but every open tab must update. What should the developer change?
options: Import `APPLICATION_SCOPE` and pass `{ scope: APPLICATION_SCOPE }` as the fourth argument to `subscribe()`
Move the `subscribe()` call from `connectedCallback()` to `renderedCallback()`
Publish the message with `{ scope: APPLICATION_SCOPE }` from the utility bar component instead
Replace the message channel with a `CustomEvent` that has `bubbles: true` and `composed: true`
questions.explain: By default, an LMS subscriber only hears messages while it's in the active area, like the focused tab. Subscribe with `{ scope: APPLICATION_SCOPE }` so components in background tabs hear them too.
wrong: `renderedCallback` runs after every render and would pile up subscriptions; scope is the real problem.
The subscriber sets the scope in `subscribe()`, not the publisher.
DOM events can't travel from the utility bar to a separate tab; they share no DOM tree.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Define the Scope of the Message Service

questions.q: A field sales team wants a "Nearby Visits" component. On Lightning app pages it must appear only on phones. On Account record pages it must appear on both desktop and phone. Which `js-meta.xml` configuration meets this?
questions.code:
<!-- Option shape -->
<targetConfigs>
  <targetConfig targets="...">
    <supportedFormFactors>
      <supportedFormFactor type="..."/>
    </supportedFormFactors>
  </targetConfig>
</targetConfigs>
options: One `targetConfig` for `"lightning__AppPage,lightning__RecordPage"` with `supportedFormFactor` `type="Small"` only
A `targetConfig` for `lightning__AppPage` with `type="Small"`, and a `targetConfig` for `lightning__RecordPage` with `type="Large"` and `type="Small"`
A `targetConfig` for `lightning__AppPage` with `type="Phone"`, and a `targetConfig` for `lightning__RecordPage` with `type="Desktop"` and `type="Phone"`
A `supportedFormFactors` block directly under `<targets>`, listing `type="Small"` for app pages and `type="Medium"` for record pages
questions.explain: Device rules go inside each `targetConfig`, so every page type can have its own devices. App pages get `Small` only. Record pages get `Large` and `Small`.
wrong: One shared `targetConfig` would limit record pages to phones too, so desktop users lose it.
`Phone` and `Desktop` aren't valid types; the values are `Small` and `Large`.
`supportedFormFactors` can't sit directly under targets, and `Medium` isn't valid for pages.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Configure Your Component for Different Form Factors

questions.q: A developer wants a compact card layout for phone users of the Salesforce mobile app and the full table on desktop. Testers on phones always see the full table. What is the bug?
options: `formFactor` must be read in `connectedCallback()`, because the module value is not ready when the getter runs
The value for a phone is `'PHONE'`, the same as `$Browser.formFactor` in Aura
The value for a phone is `'Small'`, so the getter should compare `FORM_FACTOR` to `'Small'`
Getters are not reactive, so `isPhone` must be a field decorated with `@track`
questions.explain: The LWC form factor module uses size words, not device words. `@salesforce/client/formFactor` returns `Large` (desktop), `Medium` (tablet) or `Small` (phone). So comparing to `'Phone'` is never true.
wrong: The imported value is ready as soon as the module loads, so a getter can read it anytime.
`PHONE` comes from Aura's `$Browser`, not from the LWC `formFactor` module.
The getter returns a constant, so reactivity isn't the issue, and `@track` wouldn't fix the comparison.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Client Form Factor

questions.q: On a phone, the two panels below appear squeezed side by side instead of stacked. On desktops they should sit side by side at half width each. Which two changes fix the layout? (Choose 2)
questions.code:
<lightning-layout>
  <lightning-layout-item medium-device-size="6" padding="around-small">
    <c-account-summary></c-account-summary>
  </lightning-layout-item>
  <lightning-layout-item medium-device-size="6" padding="around-small">
    <c-open-cases></c-open-cases>
  </lightning-layout-item>
</lightning-layout>
options: Replace `medium-device-size="6"` with `small-device-size="12"` only
Add `size="12"` to each `lightning-layout-item`
Add `flexibility="auto"` to `lightning-layout`
Wrap each item in a div with class `slds-hide_medium`
Add `multiple-rows="true"` to `lightning-layout` so items can wrap onto new rows
questions.explain: Device-size attributes only work when `size` is also set. `size="12"` makes each item full width on phones, and `medium-device-size="6"` takes over from tablets up. `multiple-rows="true"` lets full-width items wrap onto new rows.
wrong: `small-device-size` still needs `size` set, and it would make items full width on bigger screens too.
`flexibility` belongs on `lightning-layout-item`, and auto sizing doesn't force items to stack.
`slds-hide_medium` hides content from medium screens up, so desktops would lose the panels.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-layout-item

questions.q: An Aura component on a record page should show a short summary on phones and a detailed view on desktop. On phones it always shows the detailed view. Which two changes would make the phone check work? (Choose 2)
questions.code:
<aura:component implements="flexipage:availableForRecordHome">
  <aura:if isTrue="{!$Browser.formFactor == 'Small'}">
    <c:shortSummary/>
    <aura:set attribute="else">
      <c:detailedView/>
    </aura:set>
  </aura:if>
</aura:component>
options: Import `@salesforce/client/formFactor` in the Aura controller
Compare `$Browser.formFactor` to `'small'` in lowercase
Compare `$Browser.formFactor` to `'PHONE'`
Use `{!$Browser.isPhone}` as the condition
Add a `design:supportedFormFactor` of type `Small` to the component's `.design` file
questions.explain: Aura's `$Browser` uses its own capital-letter words. `$Browser.formFactor` returns values like `DESKTOP` and `PHONE`, and `$Browser.isPhone` is true on phones. `Small` and `Large` belong to LWC and page settings.
wrong: `@salesforce` scoped modules are for LWC, not Aura controllers.
The value is `PHONE`, so lowercasing `'Small'` doesn't help.
The `.design` file controls where App Builder offers the component, not which markup it shows.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: $Browser

questions.q: A Visualforce page styled with `apex:slds` shows a set of product tiles. Product owners want one tile per row on phones, two per row on tablets and three per row on desktops. Each tile is a div inside a parent div. Which classes should the developer use?
questions.code:
...
...
...
options: Parent: `slds-grid`; tile: `slds-size_1-of-3 slds-medium-size_1-of-2 slds-small-size_1-of-1`
Parent: `slds-container_fluid`; tile: `slds-col slds-max-small-size_1-of-1`
Parent: `slds-wrap`; tile: `slds-size_1-of-1 slds-size_1-of-2 slds-size_1-of-3`
Parent: `slds-grid slds-wrap`; tile: `slds-col slds-size_1-of-1 slds-medium-size_1-of-2 slds-large-size_1-of-3`
questions.explain: The SLDS grid is mobile first. The plain size class applies to every screen, and medium and large classes take over from those sizes up. The parent needs `slds-grid` and `slds-wrap` so tiles flow onto new rows.
wrong: Without `slds-wrap` the tiles stay in one row, and plain 1-of-3 would hit phones, the reverse of mobile first.
This only sets a phone size and never makes the two- and three-column layouts.
`slds-wrap` needs `slds-grid`, and three plain size classes on one element just conflict.
questions.source: Lightning Design System: Grid utility classes

questions.q: An Aura wrapper contains an LWC that lets agents pick a warranty plan. The LWC dispatches the event below. Which line in the Aura controller correctly reads the selected plan Id?
options: `component.get('v.planId')`
`event.getSource().get('v.selectedPlanId')`
`event.target.value`
`event.getParam('planId')`
questions.explain: When Aura handles a DOM event from an LWC, each key in the event's `detail` becomes a parameter. Read it with `event.getParam('planId')`.
wrong: This reads the wrapper's own attribute, which isn't set yet.
`selectedPlanId` is a private LWC field, not an Aura attribute, so it can't be read this way.
`event.target.value` is for native input events; the data is in the custom event's detail.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Send Events to an Enclosing Aura Component

questions.q: An Aura app page component contains an LWC with an `@api` method called `loadDefaults()`. The Aura component calls it from its init handler, but the browser console shows an error and the defaults never load. What is the cause?
questions.code:
<!-- quoteShell.cmp -->
<aura:component implements="flexipage:availableForAllPageTypes">
  <aura:handler name="init" value="{!this}" action="{!c.doInit}"/>
  <c:quoteLines aura:id="lines"/>
</aura:component>

// quoteShellController.js
doInit: function (component) {
  component.find('lines').loadDefaults();
}
options: Aura cannot call LWC methods. The LWC must listen for an Aura application event instead
The LWC is not created until the Aura component renders, so its method cannot be called during init
`aura:id` does not work on LWCs. The method must be found with `document.querySelector('c-quote-lines')`
The method name must be in kebab case, such as `component.find('lines')['load-defaults']()`
questions.explain: An LWC inside Aura doesn't exist until the Aura component renders. Aura can call its `@api` method with `component.find()`, but not during init. So the call fails.
wrong: Aura can call an LWC's public method with `component.find('auraId').methodName()`.
`aura:id` works on LWCs in Aura markup, and document queries break encapsulation.
JavaScript methods keep their camelCase name; kebab case is only for HTML attributes.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Compose Aura Components from Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A Reset button in an Aura wrapper should clear the filters in a child LWC. Clicking it throws "`component.find(...).clearFilters` is not a function". What should the developer change?
options: Decorate `clearFilters()` with `@api` so the parent can call it
Rename the method to `setClearFilters()` so Aura treats it as a setter
Fire an Aura component event from the wrapper and handle it in the LWC with `aura:handler`
Change `objectName` to a method so Aura sees the component as public
questions.explain: A parent can only call a child's method if the method is public. Decorate `clearFilters()` with `@api`. That's true whether the parent is Aura or LWC.
wrong: Aura doesn't treat methods starting with `set` as public.
An LWC can't use `aura:handler` or handle Aura component events.
One public property doesn't make other methods public; each method needs `@api`.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Compose Aura Components from Lightning Web Components

questions.q: An LWC (`c-region-picker`) sits inside Aura component A, which is inside Aura component B. The picker dispatches a `regionchange` event. Component B must react, but a handler that B puts on its `<c:componentA>` tag never runs. Which two approaches work? (Choose 2)
options: Handle `onregionchange` on the `<c:regionPicker>` tag in component A, then fire an Aura component event that B handles
Dispatch the event with `bubbles: true` and `composed: true` so B's `onregionchange` handler on `<c:componentA>` catches it
Publish the region on a Lightning message channel from the LWC and subscribe in B with `lightning:messageChannel`
Add `<aura:handler name="regionchange" action="{!c.handle}"/>` to component B
Register the event in the LWC with `<aura:registerEvent name="regionchange" type="c:regionEvt"/>`
questions.explain: An `onxxx` handler for an LWC event can only sit in the first Aura component the event reaches, here A. A can pass the news on with an Aura event. Or skip nesting entirely with Lightning Message Service, which links LWC and Aura directly.
wrong: The docs say only the first Aura component the event bubbles to can handle it, so B still can't.
A named `aura:handler` handles Aura component events, not DOM events from an LWC.
`aura:registerEvent` is Aura markup; LWCs can't fire Aura events.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Send Events to an Enclosing Aura Component

questions.q: A Visualforce page on an Account Lightning record page subscribes to a message channel that an LWC publishes on. The page updates correctly in Lightning Experience on desktop, but sales reps say it never updates in the Salesforce mobile app. What is the most likely reason?
questions.code:
<apex:page>
  <script>
    var CHANNEL = "{!$MessageChannel.Account_Selected__c}";
    var sub;
    function startListening() {
      if (!sub) {
        sub = sforce.one.subscribe(CHANNEL, onAccount, { scope: "APPLICATION" });
      }
    }
    function onAccount(msg) { /* update the page */ }
    startListening();
  </script>
</apex:page>
options: The channel must be referenced as `$MessageChannel.Account_Selected` instead of with the `__c` suffix on mobile
The `scope` option must be removed, because `APPLICATION` scope is not allowed on mobile
The LWC must publish with `sforce.one.publish()` so that the Visualforce page can receive it
Lightning Message Service supports Aura and LWC in the Salesforce mobile app, but not Visualforce pages
questions.explain: In the Salesforce mobile app, Lightning Message Service works for Aura and LWC only. Visualforce pages there can't send or receive messages. So the code is fine; the platform is the limit.
wrong: The channel API name always keeps the `__c` suffix, on every device.
Dropping the scope won't help, because LMS doesn't support Visualforce in the mobile app.
An LWC publishes with `publish()` from `lightning/messageService`; `sforce.one` is the Visualforce API.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lightning Message Service Limitations

questions.q: An Aura component must publish the selected order on the `Order_Selected__c` message channel when a button is clicked. Clicking the button throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'publish')". What is the fix?
questions.code:
<!-- orderList.cmp -->
<aura:component>
  <lightning:messageChannel type="Order_Selected__c"/>
  <lightning:button label="Select" onclick="{!c.handleSelect}"/>
</aura:component>

// orderListController.js
handleSelect: function (cmp) {
  cmp.find('orderChannel').publish({ orderId: cmp.get('v.orderId') });
}
options: Import the channel with `import ORDER from '@salesforce/messageChannel/Order_Selected__c'` in the controller
Call `$A.get('e.c:Order_Selected__c').fire()` instead of `publish()`
Add `aura:id="orderChannel"` to the `lightning:messageChannel` tag
Set `scope="APPLICATION"` on `lightning:messageChannel`
questions.explain: Aura finds its `lightning:messageChannel` by `aura:id`, then calls `publish()` on it. With no `aura:id`, `cmp.find()` returns `undefined`. Then `.publish` throws.
wrong: `@salesforce` module imports are for LWC; Aura uses the `lightning:messageChannel` tag.
A message channel isn't an Aura application event, so `$A.get()` can't fire it.
`scope` controls which subscribers hear messages; it doesn't fix the missing reference.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Publish on a Message Channel

questions.q: A developer uploaded `chart.js` as a zip static resource named `chartjs_v4`. Inside the zip the file is at `dist/chart.umd.js`. The LWC below shows the error toast on every page load, and the network tab shows a 404 for the script. What is the fix?
options: Build the path with a slash: `CHARTJS + '/dist/chart.umd.js'`
Import the file directly with `import CHARTJS from '@salesforce/resourceUrl/chartjs_v4/dist/chart.umd.js'`
Move `loadScript()` into `connectedCallback()`, because `renderedCallback()` runs too late for libraries
Upload the file again as a separate static resource, because `loadScript` cannot read files inside a zip
questions.explain: The imported URL points at the zip itself. Add the path inside it with string joining, and start that path with a slash. Without the slash the URL is wrong and returns 404.
wrong: The import names only the static resource; the inside path is added at runtime.
`renderedCallback` plus a guard flag is the documented pattern, and it doesn't cause a 404.
`loadScript` can read a file from a zip when the path is built correctly.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Static Resources

questions.q: A team is planning how to package front-end assets (a 3 MB mapping library, icons and a stylesheet) as static resources for LWC, Aura and Visualforce pages, some of which are used on a public Experience Cloud site. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: An LWC can load the library by adding `<script src={libUrl}></script>` to its template once the URL is imported
A single static resource can be up to 5 MB, and an org can hold up to 250 MB of static resources
In a Salesforce DX project, assets can be grouped into subfolders of the `staticresources` folder, one per library
With Cache Control set to Public, the cached resource can be reached by all internet traffic, including unauthenticated users
A static resource name such as `map-lib-v2` is valid as long as it is unique in the org
questions.explain: The documented limits are **5 MB** per static resource and **250 MB** per org. With Cache Control set to Public, the cached file is shared and reachable by anyone, even signed-out visitors. That matters on public sites.
wrong: LWC templates can't hold script tags; libraries load with `loadScript`.
You can't make subfolders in `staticresources`; use a zip to keep folders.
Names allow only letters, numbers and underscores, so hyphens aren't allowed.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Static Resources

questions.q: A field service Visualforce page needs a signature pad library. The developer uploaded a zip static resource named `SignaturePad` that contains `js/signature_pad.min.js`. Which markup loads the script correctly?
options: `<apex:includeScript value="{!$Resource.SignaturePad.js.signature_pad}"/>`
`<ltng:require scripts="{!$Resource.SignaturePad + '/js/signature_pad.min.js'}"/>`
`<apex:includeScript value="{!$Resource['SignaturePad/js/signature_pad.min.js']}"/>`
`<apex:includeScript value="{!URLFOR($Resource.SignaturePad, 'js/signature_pad.min.js')}"/>`
questions.explain: In Visualforce, a file inside a zip static resource needs `URLFOR()`. Pass the resource and the path inside the zip. Plain `$Resource.name` is only for stand-alone files.
wrong: Merge fields can't walk into a zip with dot notation.
`ltng:require` is an Aura tag, not used in Visualforce pages.
The `$Resource` key is the resource name only; the inside path isn't part of it.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Referencing a Static Resource in Visualforce Markup

questions.q: An Aura component draws a heat map with two libraries from the `mapLibs` zip: `leaflet.js`, and `heat.js`, which depends on leaflet. Users see "L is not defined" in the console and the map never draws. Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
questions.code: // controller doInit: function (component) { var map = L.map(component.find('map').getElement()); }
options: Put each library in its own `ltng:require` tag so they load separately and in order
Add `<script src="{!$Resource.mapLibs + '/leaflet.js'}"/>` above the `ltng:require` tag
Build the `scripts` value with `join(',', $Resource.mapLibs + '/leaflet.js', $Resource.mapLibs + '/heat.js')`
Call `loadScript()` from `lightning/platformResourceLoader` in the Aura controller instead
Remove the init handler and run the map code from `afterScriptsLoaded="{!c.initMap}"` on `ltng:require`
questions.explain: Two rules fix this. Several `$Resource` references in one attribute must be combined with `join()`. And scripts load later, so code that uses them goes in `afterScriptsLoaded`, not init.
wrong: Separate `ltng:require` tags load in parallel, so `heat.js` could load before `leaflet.js`.
Aura components can't contain script tags.
`lightning/platformResourceLoader` is an LWC module; Aura uses `ltng:require`.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Using External JavaScript Libraries

questions.q: A Lightning record page has an older Aura component that loads a charting library with `ltng:require`, and a new LWC that loads the same file with `loadScript`. Both use the same static resource URL. After the LWC renders, the Aura chart loses the plugins it had registered on the library's global object. What explains this?
options: `ltng:require` loads its scripts again each time the Aura component rerenders, which wipes the plugins it registered
Archive static resources are unpacked again on every request, which resets the global object
`ltng:require` and `loadScript` don't detect each other, so the file runs twice; load it once or check its global
Static resources with Private cache control are downloaded again for each component on the page
questions.explain: `ltng:require` and `loadScript` don't know about each other. So the same file runs twice and replaces the library's global object, plugins and all. Load it once, or have the script check for its own global first.
wrong: `ltng:require` loads each script only once, even across components.
How the zip is stored doesn't reset globals; running the script twice does.
Cache control affects server caching between users, not how often a script runs.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning/platformResourceLoader

questions.q: A component shows a renewal record with `getRecord`. When users open it for a record they cannot access, the error banner shows up empty instead of with a message. What change fixes the banner?
options: Read `error.message` instead, because wire adapters throw standard JavaScript Error objects
Read the message from `error.statusText`, because LDS puts the message there for 4xx errors
Wrap the handler in try/catch, because wire errors are thrown instead of being passed in `error`
Check `Array.isArray(error.body)` and join the message of each item, falling back to `error.body.message`
questions.explain: UI API reads like `getRecord` give `error.body` as an **array**. Apex and write errors give an object. A `reduceErrors`-style helper handles both.
wrong: LDS errors are `FetchResponse` objects with `body`, `ok`, `status` and `statusText`, not plain Errors.
`statusText` holds status text like `NOT_FOUND`, not the message for users.
The wire passes errors in the `error` property; try/catch doesn't change the body's shape.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Errors in Lightning Data Service

questions.q: A security review of a payment LWC found that when the Apex method fails, the browser receives the Apex class name and line details in `error.body.stackTrace`. The team wants users to see a short, clear message and no internal details. What should the developer do?
options: Wrap the JavaScript call in try/catch so the stack trace is not sent to the browser
Catch it in Apex and `throw new AuraHandledException('We could not apply this payment.')`
Define `PaymentException extends Exception` and throw it with the same message from a catch block
Mark the method `cacheable=true` so errors are served from the client cache without server details
questions.explain: To hide internal details, Apex must send its own message on purpose. An `AuraHandledException` returns your message, and its error has no `body.stackTrace`. Unhandled exceptions go to the client as they are.
wrong: A client try/catch runs after the browser already has the error details.
An unhandled custom exception still sends the class name and line number.
A DML method can't be cacheable, and caching doesn't hide error details anyway.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Errors from Apex

questions.q: An Aura component calls an Apex method that throws `AuraHandledException('Credit limit exceeded')`. The error toast appears, but it says "undefined". What is the bug?
options: `response.getError()` returns an array, so the message is in `errors[0].message`
`AuraHandledException` sets the state to `INCOMPLETE`, so the message is never in the `ERROR` branch
The message is only available from `response.getReturnValue()` when the state is `ERROR`
`AuraHandledException` messages are only sent to Lightning web components, not to Aura components
questions.explain: In Aura, `response.getError()` returns an **array** of error objects, not one object. The `AuraHandledException` message is in `errors[0].message`. The state is still `ERROR`.
wrong: `INCOMPLETE` means the server couldn't be reached; a thrown `AuraHandledException` gives `ERROR`.
`getReturnValue()` holds a successful result, not error details.
`AuraHandledException` was built for Aura and works for LWC too.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Returning Errors from an Apex Server-Side Controller

questions.q: On a Visualforce order page, `applyCoupon()` adds an error message when the coupon has expired. The totals panel refreshes, but users never see the error. Which two changes would show the message? (Choose 2)
questions.code:
<apex:form>
  <apex:pageMessages/>
  <apex:inputText value="{!couponCode}"/>
  <apex:commandButton value="Apply" action="{!applyCoupon}" rerender="totals"/>
  <apex:outputPanel id="totals">{!orderTotal}</apex:outputPanel>
</apex:form>

// controller
public PageReference applyCoupon() {
  if (couponIsExpired(couponCode)) {
    ApexPages.addMessage(new ApexPages.Message(
      ApexPages.Severity.ERROR, 'This coupon has expired.'));
  }
  return null;
}
options: Give `apex:pageMessages` an `id` such as `"msgs"` and set `rerender="totals,msgs"`
Add `immediate="true"` to the command button so messages are sent first
Return `new PageReference('/apex/OrderPage').setRedirect(true)` after adding the message
Change the severity to `FATAL` so the message is shown even during partial refresh
Move `apex:pageMessages` inside the totals output panel
questions.explain: A partial refresh redraws only what's in `rerender`. So the messages component must be redrawn too. Either add its id to `rerender`, or put it inside a panel that's rerendered.
wrong: `immediate` skips applying typed values, so the coupon never reaches the controller.
A redirect starts a new request, and the old messages are lost.
Severity changes the message's style, not whether it's redrawn.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:pageMessages

questions.q: A partner self-registration LWC runs in an LWR Experience Cloud site. When the Apex save fails, the catch block below runs (the console log confirms it), but no toast appears on the page. What should the developer do?
options: Add `mode: 'sticky'` so the toast stays visible until it is closed
Create the event with `bubbles: true` and `composed: true` so the site shell receives it
Import `Toast` from `'lightning/toast'` and call `Toast.show({ label, message, variant: 'error' }, this)`
Add a `lightning/toastContainer` instance to the page, because `ShowToastEvent` needs a container in LWR sites
questions.explain: `lightning/platformShowToastEvent` doesn't work in LWR Experience Cloud sites. Use `lightning/toast` there. `Toast.show()` creates its own page-level toast container.
wrong: `mode` controls how long a toast stays; in an LWR site no toast shows at all.
Event travel isn't the problem; LWR sites don't handle `ShowToastEvent`.
A toast container can't make an unsupported module work in an LWR site.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Toast Notifications

questions.q: A custom two-column `lightning-record-edit-form` saves Contracts. When a validation rule blocks the save, nothing happens on screen and users think the button is broken. The team wants server errors to show in the form automatically, without writing an error handler, and must keep its custom markup (a grid with section headings and help text between the fields). What should the developer add?
options: An `onerror` handler that dispatches a `ShowToastEvent` with `event.detail.message`
A `lightning-messages` component placed just before or after the input fields
`required` on every `lightning-input-field` so errors are caught before submit
Replace the form with `lightning-record-form`, which shows errors automatically
questions.explain: The edit form can show server errors by itself if you give it a spot. Put `lightning-messages` inside `lightning-record-edit-form`. It shows save errors, validation rules included, with no handler code.
wrong: It works, but it's a custom error handler, which the team wants to avoid.
`required` only checks for empty fields in the browser; it can't catch server validation rules.
`lightning-record-form` builds its own layout, so the custom markup would be lost.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-record-edit-form

questions.q: A custom controller page lets users update an Account. When a validation rule (error location: top of page) fails, users get a full-page Visualforce error with `FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION` instead of a friendly message on the form. Which two changes together show the error on the page? (Choose 2)
questions.code:
<apex:page controller="AccountUpdateController">
  <apex:form>
    <apex:inputField value="{!account.Name}"/>
    <apex:inputField value="{!account.Rating}"/>
    <apex:commandButton value="Save" action="{!save}"/>
  </apex:form>
</apex:page>

public PageReference save() {
  update account;
  return null;
}
options: Throw `new AuraHandledException('Please fix the errors')` from `save()`
Wrap the update in `try/catch (DmlException ex)` and call `ApexPages.addMessages(ex)`
Add `<apex:pageMessages/>` (or `apex:messages`) to the page
Return `new PageReference(ApexPages.currentPage().getUrl()).setRedirect(true)` from `save()`
Set `escape="false"` on the `inputField` components so the error text can render
questions.explain: A custom controller must handle save errors itself. Catch the `DmlException` and call `ApexPages.addMessages(ex)`. Then the page needs a messages component to show top-of-page errors.
wrong: `AuraHandledException` is for Lightning components; in Visualforce it's still unhandled.
A redirect starts a new request, so the message and the user's edits are lost.
`apex:inputField` has no `escape` attribute, and escaping isn't why the error is missing.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Validation Rules and Custom Controllers

questions.q: A related contacts LWC on the Account record page always shows "No contacts", even for accounts with many contacts. Debug logs show the Apex method runs with `accountId = 'recordId'`. What should the developer change?
options: Change the config to `{ accountId: this.recordId }`
Decorate `recordId` with `@track` as well as `@api`
Change the config to `{ accountId: '$recordId' }`
Rename the Apex parameter to `recordId` so it matches the property name
questions.explain: Without the `$`, the wire sends the literal word `'recordId'`. With `'$recordId'`, it sends the property's value. It also calls again whenever that value changes.
wrong: In a `@wire` config, `this` isn't the component, and the value wouldn't be reactive.
`@api` fields are already reactive; the problem is the literal string.
The Apex parameter must match the config key, `accountId`, which it already does.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Wire Apex Methods to Lightning Web Components

questions.q: An admin adds the "Open Cases" LWC to both the Account record page and the Home page. On the record page it works. On the Home page it shows the loading spinner forever, and no error appears in the console or the debug logs. Why?
options: The Home page has no record, so `recordId` is `undefined`, and the wire won't call Apex while a parameter is `undefined`
Apex throws a `NullPointerException` for the null Id, and cacheable methods hide server errors from the client
`@wire` only runs on record pages, so the component must call `getOpenCases` imperatively on other pages
The cached result from the record page is locked to that page, so the Home page waits until the cache entry expires
questions.explain: A wire waits while any parameter is `undefined`, and calls nothing. The Home page has no record, so `recordId` is `undefined`. No data or error ever arrives, so the spinner never stops.
wrong: Apex is never called, so there's no exception, and cacheable methods do return errors.
`@wire` works on any page; it only waits because the parameter is `undefined`.
The cache is keyed by parameters and never blocks other pages.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Wire Apex Methods to Lightning Web Components

questions.q: After a user adds a line item, the totals panel still shows the old amount until the page is reloaded. `getTotals` is `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)` and `addLine` is `@AuraEnabled` without cacheable. Which two changes would make the totals refresh? (Choose 2)
options: Call `refreshApex(this.totals)` after `addLine()` resolves
Mark `addLine` as `cacheable=true` so both methods share one cache entry and refresh each other
Decorate `totals` with `@track` so the template sees the new values
Remove `cacheable=true` from `getTotals` so every imperative call goes to the server
Wire `getTotals` with `{ quoteId: '$recordId' }`, keep the provisioned value, and pass it to `refreshApex()` after `addLine()` resolves
questions.explain: A cacheable method called imperatively checks the browser cache first. Same parameters can mean the same old answer. So make the call non-cacheable, or wire it and refresh with `refreshApex()`.
wrong: `refreshApex()` only works with a value a `@wire` handed over, not an imperative result.
`addLine` does DML, so it can't be cacheable.
The property is reassigned, so it's already reactive; the value itself is stale.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Client-Side Caching of Apex Method Results

questions.q: A product picker lets users tick products before adding them to a quote. Ticking a checkbox throws an "Invalid mutation ... is read-only" error in the console. What is the best fix?
options: Decorate `products` with `@track` so its nested properties can be changed
Copy the records as they arrive: `this.products = data.map((p) => ({ ...p, selected: false }))`
Call `refreshApex()` before changing the record so the wire cache is unlocked and the objects become writable
Move the assignment of `this.products` into `renderedCallback()`
questions.explain: Data from the wire service is read-only. To change it, make your own copy first. A shallow copy with an extra `selected` flag works.
wrong: `@track` doesn't make the wire's read-only objects writable.
`refreshApex()` fetches fresh data, which is read-only too.
Where you assign doesn't matter; the objects themselves are read-only.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Understand the Wire Service

questions.q: An order dashboard LWC displays the result of the Apex method below. The order number and total show correctly, but the Status column is always empty, even though debug logs show `status` is set on every object. What is the cause?
options: The `status` property is not annotated with `@AuraEnabled`, so it is not serialized to the client
Status is a restricted picklist, so it must be converted with `String.valueOf()` first
Wrapper classes must be declared `without sharing` for all their properties to be returned
The query needs `WITH USER_MODE`, otherwise picklist fields are removed from wrapper objects
questions.explain: Only Apex properties marked `@AuraEnabled` are sent to the browser. `status` lacks the annotation. So the client never gets it, and the column stays empty.
wrong: `Order.Status` is already a String in Apex; no conversion is needed.
Sharing affects which records return, not which properties are sent.
`USER_MODE` enforces permissions; it doesn't decide which wrapper properties are sent.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Returning Data from an Apex Server-Side Controller

questions.q: Compliance wants every view of the pricing panel to be logged. A developer adds an insert to the wired Apex method below. Now the panel shows an error instead of prices. Which change meets both needs and keeps the wire?
options: Use `Database.insert(log, false)` so a failed insert does not stop the query or the wire from returning
Declare the class `without sharing` so the insert is allowed in a cacheable method
Keep `getPrices` read-only and log the view in a separate non-cacheable method called imperatively
Pass `{ cacheable: false }` in the `@wire` configuration object for this call
questions.explain: A cacheable method may only read, so it can't do DML. Keep `getPrices` read-only for the wire. Log the view in a separate non-cacheable method called imperatively.
wrong: `Database.insert` is still DML, which a cacheable method can't do.
Sharing doesn't change the no-DML rule for cacheable methods.
The wire config only passes parameters; cacheability lives on the annotation, and `@wire` needs `cacheable=true`.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Client-Side Caching of Apex Method Results

questions.q: A shipping-rate LWC uses a Continuation because the carrier API can take up to 40 seconds. The component wires `startRequest`. What happens when the component loads?
options: It works, but the response is not cached on the client
It fails to compile, because `continuation=true` and `cacheable=true` must be separated by a comma in `@AuraEnabled`
It works only for imperative calls, and the wire silently provisions nothing
It throws an exception: if the Continuation method is cacheable, the callback must be `cacheable=true` too
questions.explain: In a Continuation chain, cacheable settings must match. A cacheable starting method with a non-cacheable callback is invalid and throws an exception. Mark every method in the chain `cacheable=true` to make it work with `@wire`.
wrong: The docs list this exact combination as invalid; it doesn't just skip caching.
The attributes are separated by a space, as written: `continuation=true cacheable=true`.
The combination is invalid, so it isn't about wire versus imperative.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: @AuraEnabled Annotations for Continuations

questions.q: On a Visualforce page for Opportunity, changing Stage should redraw the forecast panel. Instead, users who have not entered a Close Date yet see "Close Date: You must enter a value" and the panel does not update. What should the developer do?
questions.code:
<apex:page standardController="Opportunity" extensions="ForecastExt">
  <apex:form>
    <apex:pageBlock id="block">
      <apex:inputField value="{!Opportunity.CloseDate}"/>
      <apex:inputField value="{!Opportunity.StageName}">
        <apex:actionSupport event="onchange" action="{!recalcForecast}" rerender="forecast"/>
      </apex:inputField>
      <apex:outputPanel id="forecast">{!forecastText}</apex:outputPanel>
    </apex:pageBlock>
  </apex:form>
</apex:page>
options: Add `immediate="true"` to the `actionSupport` so validation is skipped
Change `rerender="forecast"` to `rerender="block"` so the whole block is redrawn
Set `required="false"` on the Close Date `inputField`
Wrap the Stage `inputField` and its `actionSupport` in an `apex:actionRegion`
questions.explain: `apex:actionRegion` limits which fields the server processes in an AJAX request. Wrap Stage in it. Then only Stage is sent and checked, so the empty Close Date can't block it.
wrong: `immediate` skips validation but also drops the new Stage, so the forecast uses stale data.
`rerender` controls what's redrawn, not what's processed, so the error stays.
Close Date is required on Opportunity, and the business still needs it on save.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionRegion

questions.q: Sales reps change the quantity, then click Recalculate. The summary panel redraws, but it still shows the totals for the old quantity. What is the cause?
questions.code:
<apex:inputText value="{!quantity}"/>
<apex:commandButton value="Recalculate" action="{!recalculate}"
                    immediate="true" rerender="summary"/>
<apex:outputPanel id="summary">Total: {!total}</apex:outputPanel>

// controller
public Integer quantity { get; set; }
public Decimal total { get; private set; }
public PageReference recalculate() {
  total = quantity * unitPrice;
  return null;
}
options: `total` has a private setter, so the page cannot show the new value
`immediate="true"` skips updating the data model, so the quantity setter never gets the new value
`rerender` only works on `apex:outputPanel` elements that also have `layout="block"`, so the panel keeps old values
`inputText` cannot bind to an Integer property; it must use `apex:inputField`
questions.explain: `immediate="true"` runs the action without saving the typed values to the controller. So `recalculate()` still sees the old quantity. `immediate` is meant for leaving actions like Cancel.
wrong: A private setter only stops the page writing `total`; the controller can still set it.
`rerender` works on any component with an id, whatever its layout.
`apex:inputText` can bind to plain properties like an Integer.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Use the immediate Attribute Carefully

questions.q: A developer wants a Remove button on each row of an order lines table, using the markup below in a page at API version 60.0. The markup breaks a rule for `apex:actionFunction`. Which change fixes it?
questions.code: {!l.Name}
options: Replace the `actionFunction` with a `@RemoteAction` method, which can rerender the lines panel
Add `immediate="true"` to the `actionFunction` so the parameter is assigned first
Move the `apex:actionFunction` after the `apex:repeat`, still inside the `apex:form`
Move the `apex:actionFunction` outside the `apex:form` so it is defined only once
questions.explain: Since API version 23, `apex:actionFunction` can't sit inside an iteration component. Define it once after the `apex:repeat`, still inside the form. Then call it from each row with the parameter.
wrong: Remote actions are static and can't rerender Visualforce components.
`immediate` would skip applying values, and the placement problem would stay.
`apex:actionFunction` must be inside an `apex:form`.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionFunction

questions.q: A warranty lookup button on a Visualforce page calls a slow external service that takes about 20 seconds. At month end, hundreds of agents click it at once and many get errors about too many concurrent long-running requests. What should the developer change in the controller?
options: Return a Continuation from the action, with `continuationMethod` set to a callback that reads the response
Move the callout into an `@future(callout=true)` method and set `warrantyStatus` from it
Lower `req.setTimeout()` to 5000 so each request finishes faster
Call the method with JavaScript remoting and `{ timeout: 120000 }` so the wait runs outside the page request
questions.explain: A **Continuation** hands the slow callout to a separate server and pauses the request. So it doesn't count toward the concurrent long-running request limit. A callback method reads the response when it arrives.
wrong: A future method runs later in its own transaction and can't update the waiting page.
A shorter timeout makes calls fail sooner; it doesn't speed up the service.
The server still holds the request open while it waits, so it's still long-running.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Make Long-Running Callouts with Continuations

questions.q: A tag picker shows "`{count}` selected". Users tick tags, but the count stays at 0. What should the developer change?
options: Replace `@track` with `@api` so the parent component can observe the `Set` and push its new size back down to the child
After each change, assign a new `Set`, e.g. `this.selected = new Set(this.selected)`, as `Set` mutations aren't observed
Move the `add()` and `delete()` calls into `renderedCallback()` so that every change happens inside the render cycle
Keep `@track` and add `this.selected = this.selected` after each change so the engine sees an assignment to the field
questions.explain: LWC watches plain objects and arrays, but not changes inside a `Set`, `Map`, `Date` or class instance, even with `@track`. Assigning a new `Set` gives the field a new reference. Then the component re-renders.
wrong: `@api` makes the property public and read-only to the child; it doesn't make `Set` changes visible.
Changing state in `renderedCallback` is an anti-pattern, and it still mutates the same unwatched `Set`.
Assigning the same reference equals the old value, so nothing re-renders.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Field Reactivity

questions.q: A reviewer flags the list template below. Contacts can be added and removed, and the first and last rows get special styling. What should change?
options: Use a unique value from the data as the key, such as `key={it.value.Id}`, since the index can't be a key
Move `key={it.index}` from the `li` element onto the `template` tag that holds the `iterator` directive
Replace `iterator` with `for:each`, because the `iterator` directive doesn't support `lwc:if` on its items
Replace `it.last` with a check of `it.index` against `contacts.length - 1`, because the `iterator` has no `last` property
questions.explain: Every list item needs a key: a unique string or number from the data. The docs say the index can't be the key. The iterator still gives you `value`, `index`, `first` and `last`.
wrong: The `key` goes on the first element inside the template, and an index still isn't allowed.
`lwc:if` works inside an `iterator`; `first` and `last` are why you pick `iterator`.
The iterator does offer `first` and `last` as booleans.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Render Lists

questions.q: A child LWC must round the amount its parent passes in, every time the parent changes it. The developer writes the code below, and the component fails to save. What is the fix?
options: Remove the getter, because a public property only needs a setter when the parent is the one that writes it
Rename `_amount` to `amount`, so the getter and the setter share the public property as their own backing field
Replace both with `@track amount` and do the rounding once in `connectedCallback()` when the component loads
Keep `@api` on only one of the two, by convention the getter, because a getter and setter can't both have it
questions.explain: A public property with a custom setter also needs a getter. Put `@api` on only one of them. The docs put it on the getter and keep the value in a private field like `_amount`.
wrong: A public property's setter needs a matching getter.
Using the property's own name as its store would loop into the getter and setter forever.
`connectedCallback` runs once, so later changes wouldn't be rounded, and `@track` isn't public.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Use Getters and Setters to Modify Data

questions.q: Two agents often edit the same Case in this custom LWC. The business wants a save to fail, instead of silently overwriting, if someone else saved the Case after the component loaded it. What should the developer do?
options: Call `notifyRecordUpdateAvailable([this.recordId])` just before `updateRecord`, so LDS loads the latest copy of the Case first
Add `apiName: 'Case'` to the `recordInput`, so the UI API compares record versions before it applies the update
Wire `LastModifiedDate` with `getRecord` and pass `{ ifUnmodifiedSince: lastModifiedDate }` as `updateRecord`'s `clientOptions`
Call `refreshApex` on the wired record before saving, then compare the old and new Status values in JavaScript
questions.explain: To refuse a save if someone else saved first, tell the server what version you saw. Pass `clientOptions` with `ifUnmodifiedSince` set to the `LastModifiedDate` from a wire adapter. If the record changed since, the update fails.
wrong: This refreshes the cache but still overwrites the other agent's save.
`apiName` is only for creating records; for an update, pass null or leave it out.
`refreshApex` is for wired Apex, not `getRecord`, and a JS comparison still leaves a race.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: updateRecord(recordInput, clientOptions)

questions.q: A deal summary LWC wires `getRecord` for Opportunity Amount and `CloseDate` and shows them with `getFieldValue`. Users see 125000 and 2026-12-31 instead of formatted currency and dates. The team wants formatted, localized values with no formatting code. What should the developer do?
options: Move both fields into `optionalFields`, because optional fields are returned already formatted for display to the user
Show the values with `getFieldDisplayValue(this.deal.data, AMOUNT_FIELD)`, which returns the formatted display value
Switch the wire to `layoutTypes: ['Full']`, which returns every field on the layout as a formatted string
Pass `{ formatted: true }` as a third argument to `getFieldValue`, so it returns the display value instead
questions.explain: `getFieldValue` gives the raw value; `getFieldDisplayValue` gives the formatted, localized one. Use the display version for currency and dates. The same value is also at `record.data.fields.Amount.displayValue`.
wrong: `optionalFields` only changes what happens with hidden fields; it doesn't format values.
`layoutTypes` chooses which fields come back, not whether they're formatted.
`getFieldValue` has no formatting option; `getFieldDisplayValue` is the separate function.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: getFieldDisplayValue(record, field)

questions.q: A Quick Note button in an LWC on an Account page must create a Task related to the Account with Lightning Data Service and no Apex. Which call is correct?
options: `createRecord(TASK_OBJECT, { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId })`
`updateRecord({ apiName: 'Task', fields: { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })`
`createRecord({ fields: { attributes: { type: 'Task' }, Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })`
`createRecord({ apiName: 'Task', fields: { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })`
questions.explain: `createRecord` takes one object: the `apiName` of the object plus a `fields` map. `updateRecord` only changes existing records, found by the Id in `fields`.
wrong: `createRecord` takes one `recordInput` object, not the object and fields as separate arguments.
`updateRecord` never creates records; for an update, leave out `apiName` and include the Id.
The object is named with `apiName`, not an `attributes` block inside `fields`.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: createRecord(recordInput); updateRecord(recordInput, clientOptions)

questions.q: A Visualforce page shows only `{!opportunity.Name}` and `{!maxDiscount}`. It fails with "SObject row was retrieved via SOQL without querying the requested field: `Opportunity.Amount`". Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
options: Call `std.addFields(new List<String>{ 'Amount', 'Discount_Cap__c' })` in the constructor before `getRecord()`
Declare the extension `without sharing`, so the standard controller is allowed to load every field on the record
Reference both fields on the page in a hidden component, such as an `apex:outputText` with `rendered="false"`
Call `std.reset()` inside `getMaxDiscount()` just before reading the fields, so the record is queried again in full
Read the record with `std.getRecord().clone(true, true)`, because a deep clone copies every field from the database
questions.explain: A standard controller loads only the fields the page markup uses. Call `addFields()` in the constructor to load more. Or reference the fields in a hidden component (`rendered="false"`), the documented workaround.
wrong: Sharing keywords control record access, not which fields the controller loads.
`reset()` is only needed before `addFields` outside the constructor; alone it adds no fields.
`clone()` copies fields already in memory; it doesn't query new ones.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: StandardController Class (addFields, getRecord)

questions.q: A Visualforce mass-update page builds its `StandardSetController` from `Database.getQueryLocator` over open Cases. In a large org the query matches 14,000 Cases, and the page fails with a `LimitException`. What explains it?
options: A set controller pages at most 500 records at a time, and calling `setPageSize()` above 500 throws a `LimitException`
Query locators are capped at 50,000 rows in Visualforce, and every row also counts toward the view state
Iteration components show 1,000 rows unless `readOnly="true"`, and the overflow surfaces as a `LimitException`
The set controller handles 10,000 records; a query locator returning more throws, while a List is truncated
questions.explain: A `StandardSetController` holds at most **10,000** records. Built from a query locator that returns more, it throws a `LimitException`. Built from a bigger List, it quietly cuts it to 10,000.
wrong: There's no 500-record page size limit; the total size of the set is the problem.
The 10,000 cap applies whatever the query locator's own limit, and this isn't about view state.
The 1,000-row limit is real, but it raises a collection size error on render, not this.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: StandardSetController Class

questions.q: A security review flags the Visualforce page and controller below. Which risk did it find, and what is the fix?
questions.code:
<apex:page controller="CleanupController" action="{!removeContact}"/>

public with sharing class CleanupController {
    public PageReference removeContact() {
        Id cid = ApexPages.currentPage().getParameters().get('cid');
        delete [SELECT Id FROM Contact WHERE Id = :cid];
        return Page.CleanupDone;
    }
}
options: SOQL injection through the `cid` parameter; wrap it in `String.escapeSingleQuotes()` before using it in the query
CSRF: another site can send users here and the delete runs on load; delete only from a confirmed button click
XSS through `cid`; call `HTMLENCODE` on the parameter in the controller before using it in the query
Clickjacking: turn on clickjack protection for Visualforce pages, which stops the delete when the page is framed
questions.explain: A page's `action` runs on load, before any anti-CSRF token check. So a link on any site can make a signed-in user delete records: that's **CSRF**. Never do DML in a page action; require a click, like a confirm button.
wrong: The parameter is a bind variable, which is already safe from SOQL injection.
`HTMLENCODE` is an output function, and the problem is the unasked delete, not display.
Clickjack protection stops framing, but a plain link or redirect still runs the delete.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF); Secure Coding Guide

questions.q: Agents type notes with bold text and links in a rich text field. An LWC must show the formatted notes without opening an XSS hole. What should the developer use?
options: A div with `lwc:dom="manual"` whose `innerHTML` is set to the notes in `renderedCallback()`
`<lightning-formatted-rich-text value={notes}>`, which keeps allowed tags and strips the rest
A triple-brace binding such as `{{{notes}}}` in the template, so the HTML renders as markup
`<lightning-formatted-text value={notes} linkify>`, so that the HTML tags render as formatting
questions.explain: To show user HTML safely, let a component clean it first. `lightning-formatted-rich-text` keeps only allowed tags and attributes, which blocks XSS. Writing user data to `innerHTML` skips that cleaning.
wrong: `innerHTML` with user content is exactly how script injection happens.
LWC templates have no raw-HTML binding syntax.
`lightning-formatted-text` shows plain text and links; it doesn't render HTML formatting.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-formatted-rich-text
